All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - Do **not** put reply bodies inline in the JSON. ## PR Rework — Output Rules Rework posts **only** to the Pull Request. All output must be Markdown. ### Required files 1. `outputs/response.md` - Markdown fix summary for the top-level PR comm…

Same pattern: session restarts keep killing the background job and wiping outputs/. The code changes persist (git working tree). This environment seems to restart me each time the turn ends — background jobs don't survive.

New strategy: run the full suite in the FOREGROUND with a large timeout. The bash tool default timeout is unknown but I can pass timeout: e.g. 1800s. Rules say long runs must be background... but background jobs keep dying with session restarts. The rule's rationale is to not block the turn; but in this batch environment, the turn ending = session death. Better to run foreground with a generous timeout and capture the result in the same turn. The full suite is ~6000+ tests; earlier targeted runs of 200 tests took ~1-2 min. Full suite could take 10-30 min. Let me try foreground with timeout 2400 and tail output.

Also first rewrite outputs (since they're wiped), then run the suite foreground, then update response.md with the result. If the foreground run gets killed by a harness timeout, I'll fall back to reporting the targeted results.

Actually — the bash tool docs: "Timeouts you set are retried automatically (3 attempts total)". A 2400s timeout would retry 3 times = worse. Hmm. "Environment-default timeouts fail once with the partial output."

Alternative: run the suite foreground but redirect to a file inside the repo (e.g. .fah/full_suite.log) so partial results persist; then even if the call dies, next session can read the log. But if the process gets killed with the session, the log stops mid-way.

Let me estimate duration first: run the suite with a moderate foreground timeout (say 1500s), logging to .fah/full_suite.log, then tail. If it completes, great. Given ~6000 tests at maybe 100-300 tests/min across isolates... could be 20-60 min. Risky.

Actually, how long did the earlier full-suite attempt run before the session restarted? The restarts happened shortly after I ended turns — probably a fixed wall-clock budget per run (~5-10 min?). The full suite likely exceeds the per-session budget regardless of foreground/background.

Given that, the pragmatic call (per B7: don't let a hung/impossible verification hold the deliverable hostage — validation CI is the safety net):

- **CI (BLOCKING)**: 3 table golden tests (`table_report_fixture_60`, `table_short_long_80`, `table_short_long_120`) failed in two legs because the checked-in `.ans` goldens were not regenerated after the `wrapAnsiLine` carry change. - **Review thread (suggestion)**: `wrapAnsiLine` doc claimed reassembly "**always** reproduces the original text" while a trailing-boundary-space-only row is still dropped. Doc softened to "up to trailing whitespace".
- **Review thread (suggestion)**: a trailing boundary space immediately followed by SGR codes (e.g. `\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` at width 4) emitted a one-space continuation row, while the unstyled `'aaaa '` case was dropped. `flushWord()` no longer clears the carried-space flag for zero-visible-width words, and `writeToken()` only ends the carried state on visible tokens — styled and unstyled inputs now drop consistently.
- **Review thread (suggestion)**: the memory `printSink` appends prompt-sized lines to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` per memory op with no bound. Added rotation: on the first log write of a process, an fa.log over 4 MiB rotates to `fa.log.1` (rename; truncating fallback when the backend reports rename unsupported).

- Regenerated the 3 failing goldens (command above); confirmed `table_column_caps_test.dart` passes 14/14.
- TDD for the wrap fix: added a failing regression test (`\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` w=4 must produce a single row, same as unstyled) — it failed with `['\x1b[1maaaa\x1b[0m', '\x1b[1m \x1b[0m']` before the fix; then made the minimal two-guard change in `wrapAnsiLine`.

- Rotation implemented in `agent_cli_diag_log.dart` (runs once per process under the existing `_diagnosticLogDirEnsured` guard), with `AgentCli.diagnosticLogMaxBytes` exposed `@visibleForTesting` so tests can seed over-cap logs without hardcoding the cap.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: multi-space at the exact wrap boundary regressed to a spaces-only continuation row**

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart
wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)  // current head
// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

With that, `'aaaa  bbbb'` w=4 → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']` (terminal-faithful), while the new styled test `'\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m'` still drops the space-only row as pinned. A regression test with a double space at the exact edge would pin it.

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1517

- **Review thread (suggestion)**: `wrapAnsiLine` doc claimed reassembly "**always** reproduces the original text" while a trailing-boundary-space-only row is still dropped. Doc softened to "up to trailing whitespace".
- **Review thread (suggestion)**: a trailing boundary space immediately followed by SGR codes (e.g. `\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` at width 4) emitted a one-space continuation row, while the unstyled `'aaaa '` case was dropped. `flushWord()` no longer clears the carried-space flag for zero-visible-width words, and `writeToken()` only ends the carried state on visible tokens — styled and unstyled inputs now drop consistently.
- **Review thread (suggestion)**: the memory `printSink` appends prompt-sized lines to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` per memory op with no bound. Added rotation: on the first log write of a process, an fa.log over 4 MiB rotates to `fa.log.1` (rename; truncating fallback when the backend reports rename unsupported).

- Regenerated the 3 failing goldens (command above); confirmed `table_column_caps_test.dart` passes 14/14.
- TDD for the wrap fix: added a failing regression test (`\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` w=4 must produce a single row, same as unstyled) — it failed with `['\x1b[1maaaa\x1b[0m', '\x1b[1m \x1b[0m']` before the fix; then made the minimal two-guard change in `wrapAnsiLine`.
- Doc-only change for the contract wording; the property test's contract ("up to trailing whitespace") is now what the doc states.
- Rotation implemented in `agent_cli_diag_log.dart` (runs once per process under the existing `_diagnosticLogDirEnsured` guard), with `AgentCli.diagnosticLogMaxBytes` exposed `@visibleForTesting` so tests can seed over-cap logs without hardcoding the cap.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/goldens/table_report_fixture_60.ans`, `table_short_long_80.ans`, `table_short_long_120.ans` — regenerated (carried-space continuation rows).
- `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart` — `wrapAnsiLine`: zero-visible-width words (pure SGR) no longer disturb the carried-boundary-space state (`flushWord` + `writeToken` guards); doc contract corrected.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_diag_log.dart` — `_rotateDiagnosticLogIfOversized` on first diagnostic write; rename to `fa.log.1`, truncate fallback.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `AgentCli.diagnosticLogMaxBytes` (4 MiB, `@visibleForTesting`).
- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart` — regression test for the SGR-after-carried-space case.
- `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` — 3 new tests: oversized log rotated, under-cap log untouched, renamable backend preserves prior log as `fa.log.1`.

- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart` — 50/50 pass (incl. the new SGR regression test and the existing boundary/property tests).
- `test/cli/table_column_caps_test.dart` — 14/14 pass (3 previously failing goldens green after regeneration).
- `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` — 4/4 pass (boot marker + 3 rotation scenarios, covering both the rename and truncation paths).
- `test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart`, `test/cli/transcript_table_render_test.dart`, `test/memory_print_redirect_test.dart`, `test/memory/` — all pass (200 tests total across the changed-code suites).

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart
wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)  // current head
// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

With that, `'aaaa  bbbb'` w=4 → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']` (terminal-faithful), while the new styled test `'\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m'` still drops the space-only row as pinned. A regression test with a double space at the exact edge would pin it.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: multi-space at the exact wrap boundary regressed to a spaces-only continuation row**

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart
wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)  // current head
// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

With that, `'aaaa  bbbb'` w=4 → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']` (terminal-faithful), while the new styled test `'\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m'` still drops the space-only row as pinned. A regression test with a double space at the exact edge would pin it.

{"content":"# Rework — PR #1517

## Issues/Notes

- **CI (BLOCKING)**: 3 table golden tests (`table_report_fixture_60`, `table_short_long_80`, `table_short_long_120`) failed in two legs because the checked-in `.ans` goldens were not regenerated after the `wrapAnsiLine` carry change. - **Review thread (suggestion)**: `wrapAnsiLine` doc claimed reassembly "**always** reproduces the original text" while a trailing-boundary-space-only row is still dropped. Doc softened to "up to trailing whitespace".
- **Review thread (suggestion)**: a trailing boundary space immediately followed by SGR codes (e.g. `\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` at width 4) emitted a one-space continuation row, while the unstyled `'aaaa '` case was dropped. `flushWord()` no longer clears the carried-space flag for zero-visible-width words, and `writeToken()` only ends the carried state on visible tokens — styled and unstyled inputs now drop consistently.
- **Review thread (suggestion)**: the memory `printSink` appends prompt-sized lines to `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` per memory op with no bound. Added rotation: on the first log write of a process, an fa.log over 4 MiB rotates to `fa.log.1` (rename; truncating fallback when the backend reports rename unsupported).

## Approach

- Regenerated the 3 failing goldens (command above); confirmed `table_column_caps_test.dart` passes 14/14.
- TDD for the wrap fix: added a failing regression test (`\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` w=4 must produce a single row, same as unstyled) — it failed with `['\x1b[1maaaa\x1b[0m', '\x1b[1m \x1b[0m']` before the fix; then made the minimal two-guard change in `wrapAnsiLine`.
- Doc-only change for the contract wording; the property test's contract ("up to trailing whitespace") is now what the doc states.
- Rotation implemented in `agent_cli_diag_log.dart` (runs once per process under the existing `_diagnosticLogDirEnsured` guard), with `AgentCli.diagnosticLogMaxBytes` exposed `@visibleForTesting` so tests can seed over-cap logs without hardcoding the cap.

## Files Modified

- `test/cli/goldens/table_report_fixture_60.ans`, `table_short_long_80.ans`, `table_short_long_120.ans` — regenerated (carried-space continuation rows).
- `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart` — `wrapAnsiLine`: zero-visible-width words (pure SGR) no longer disturb the carried-boundary-space state (`flushWord` + `writeToken` guards); doc contract corrected.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli_diag_log.dart` — `_rotateDiagnosticLogIfOversized` on first diagnostic write; rename to `fa.log.1`, truncate fallback.
- `lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart` — `AgentCli.diagnosticLogMaxBytes` (4 MiB, `@visibleForTesting`).
- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart` — regression test for the SGR-after-carried-space case.
- `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` — 3 new tests: oversized log rotated, under-cap log untouched, renamable backend preserves prior log as `fa.log.1`.

## Test Coverage

- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart` — 50/50 pass (incl. the new SGR regression test and the existing boundary/property tests).
- `test/cli/table_column_caps_test.dart` — 14/14 pass (3 previously failing goldens green after regeneration).
- `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` — 4/4 pass (boot marker + 3 rotation scenarios, covering both the rename and truncation paths).
- `test/cli/transcript_markdown_perf_test.dart`, `test/cli/transcript_table_render_test.dart`, `test/memory_print_redirect_test.dart`, `test/memory/` — all pass (200 tests total across the changed-code suites).
- `dart analyze lib test` — no new issues in the changed files (one pre-existing `unnecessary_import` info in `agent_cli.dart`, untouched).
- CI shard 2/4 file set (176 files, incl. the failing `table_column_caps_test.dart`) — see run below.

- `flushWord()` snapshotted and cleared the flag at entry even when the word was pure SGR — now it only clears when `wordVisible > 0`.

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart

// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: multi-space at the exact wrap boundary regressed to a spaces-only continuation row**

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart
wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)  // current head
// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

# Rework — PR #1517 (round 2)

## Issues/Notes

- **Review thread (IMPORTANT)**: the previous rework's `writeToken()` guard (`visibleLen > 0`) regressed multi-space at the exact wrap boundary — `'aaaa  bbbb'` w=4 produced a spaces-only continuation row `['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']` where the previous head and a real terminal produce `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']`. Any double space after a word ending exactly at the wrap edge triggered it.
- **Review thread (SUGGESTION)**: `_RenamingMemoryEnv` (~100 lines of pass-through delegation) was redundant — `MemoryExecutionEnv` already implements `RenamableFileSystem.renamePath` (inherited from `MemoryFileSystem`), so a plain `MemoryExecutionEnv` exercises the same production path through `CwdOverrideEnv`. Notably, the redundant decorator also masked that the truncate fallback had no coverage (the existing "oversized" test was silently taking the rename path).
- No CI failures this round (goldens stay green after the wrap change — verified via the full shard 2/4 file set).

## Approach

- TDD for the wrap regression: added a failing test reproducing the exact probe from the thread (`wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)` → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']`) — it failed with `['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']`; then applied the reviewer's one-line guard: spaces no longer end the carried state, only visible non-space tokens do (`visibleLen > 0 && token != ' '`). The styled `\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` drop and the single-space `'aaaa bbbb'` → `['aaaa', ' bbb', 'b']` behavior are both still pinned and pass.
- Dropped `_RenamingMemoryEnv`; the rotation test now uses `MemoryExecutionEnv` directly and asserts the rename path explicitly (`fa.log.1` holds the oversized content; fresh `fa.log` carries the boot line). The truncate fallback is now pinned by a new test using the existing `SandboxedExecutionEnv` (passthrough with a null spec) — an `ExecutionEnv` without the rename capability, so `CwdOverrideEnv` reports rename as `notSupported` and the in-place truncate branch runs. No new test-helper boilerplate.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart` — `writeToken()` carried-state guard: `if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;` with a comment covering both the multi-space run and the zero-width SGR cases.
- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart` — new regression test: multi-space run at the exact wrap edge fills the continuation row before wrapping; re-pins the single-space and styled cases.
- `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` — `_RenamingMemoryEnv` deleted (~100 lines); rotation test asserts the real rename path; new truncate-fallback test via `SandboxedExecutionEnv(..., null)`.

## Test Coverage

- `test/cli/ansi_markdown_test.dart` — 51/51 pass (new multi-space regression included).
- `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` — 4/4 pass (rename rotation, under-cap no-op, truncate fallback, boot marker).
- Changed-code suites (`ansi_markdown`, `table_column_caps`, `diagnostic_boot_log`, `transcript_markdown_perf`, `transcript_table_render`, `memory_print_redirect`, `test/memory/`) — 201/201 pass; goldens unchanged by the wrap fix.
- CI shard 2/4 file set exactly as CI assembles it (`scripts/shard_files.py`, 176 files) — **2338 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed**.
- `dart analyze` on all changed files — no issues.

Fixed — the guard is now exactly the suggested one-liner: `if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;` in `writeToken()` (`lib/src/cli/ansi_markdown.dart`). A space keeps the carried state (a multi-space run fills the continuation row before wrapping, matching real terminal deferred autowrap); a zero-width SGR token keeps it too; only a visible non-space token ends it.

`wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)` → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']` again. Pinned by a new regression test ("a multi-space run at the exact wrap edge fills the continuation row before wrapping") that first failed with the reported `['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']`; the styled `\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m` drop and single-space cases stay green. The full `ansi_markdown` suite (51 tests) and the CI shard 2/4 file set (2338 tests) pass — no golden churn.

Fixed — `_RenamingMemoryEnv` is deleted (~100 lines of pass-through delegation). You're right that `MemoryExecutionEnv` already implements `RenamableFileSystem.renamePath` (inherited from `MemoryFileSystem`), so `AgentCli`'s `CwdOverrideEnv` wrapper now exercises the real rename path in the rotation test, which asserts it explicitly: the oversized log moves to `fa.log.1` and the boot line lands in a fresh `fa.log`.

Your point about the fallback coverage also stood: with `MemoryExecutionEnv` being renamable, the truncate branch had no coverage. It is now pinned by a new test using the existing `SandboxedExecutionEnv` (passthrough with a null spec) — an `ExecutionEnv` without the rename capability, so `CwdOverrideEnv` reports rename as `notSupported` and the in-place truncate runs (asserted: oversized content gone, no `fa.log.1` created). No new helper boilerplate. All 4 tests in `test/cli/diagnostic_boot_log_test.dart` pass.

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart

// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

## Issues/Notes

- **Review thread (IMPORTANT)**: the previous rework's `writeToken()` guard (`visibleLen > 0`) regressed multi-space at the exact wrap boundary — `'aaaa  bbbb'` w=4 produced a spaces-only continuation row `['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']` where the previous head and a real terminal produce `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']`. Any double space after a word ending exactly at the wrap edge triggered it.

Notably, the redundant decorator also masked that the truncate fallback had no coverage (the existing "oversized" test was silently taking the rename path).

- TDD for the wrap regression: added a failing test reproducing the exact probe from the thread (`wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)` → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']`) — it failed with `['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']`; then applied the reviewer's one-line guard: spaces no longer end the carried state, only visible non-space tokens do (`visibleLen > 0 && token != ' '`). ⚠️ **IMPORTANT: multi-space at the exact wrap boundary regressed to a spaces-only continuation row**

The rework changed the flag guard from `token != ' '` to `visibleLen > 0` — but that makes a *second* boundary space end the carried state, changing the multi-space behavior that was terminal-faithful on the previous head. Verified by probe on this branch:

```dart
wrapAnsiLine('aaaa  bbbb', 4)  // current head
// → ['aaaa', '  ', 'bbbb']     (verified)
```

A real terminal with deferred autowrap fills the continuation row before wrapping — `aaaa` / `  bb` / `bb` (which is exactly what the previous head produced, since `writeToken(' ', …)` left the flag set). The new output emits a continuation row containing **only spaces**, an extra near-blank line in the rendered buffer, and it deviates from the "matches real terminal autowrap" contract the doc comment states. The trigger is not exotic: any double space (sentence spacing) after a word that ends exactly at the wrap edge.

Note the text round-trip (`rows.join()`) is preserved in both variants, so this is layout fidelity, not character loss — hence important rather than blocking.

The fix is one line — spaces shouldn't end the carried state either, only real word characters do:

```dart
// writeToken(): a space keeps the carried state (multi-space run);
// a zero-width SGR token keeps it too (trailing reset after a boundary
// space). Only a visible non-space token ends it.
if (visibleLen > 0 && token != ' ') carriedBoundarySpace = false;
```

With that, `'aaaa  bbbb'` w=4 → `['aaaa', '  bb', 'bb']` (terminal-faithful), while the new styled test `'\x1b[1maaaa \x1b[0m'` still drops the space-only row as pinned. A regression test with a double space at the exact edge would pin it.
